newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds higher, break key levels.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds higher, break key levels.

text.p: Argentine bonds were higher late morning Monday, with sentiment boosted by prices breaking key resistance levels.
"The market has broken key levels," said a trader at a foreign bank in Buenos Aires.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/4 to reach the important 90 level. The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.15 to 126.
Traders said the main factor motivating the gains this morning were further rises in U.S. Treasuries. The U.S. 30-year bond yield fell two basis points to 6.76 percent.
U.S. Treasuries rose on the release of the January National Purchasing Managers index which showed a lower-than-expected reading of 52.0.
